How the skeleton falls apart when hubs are removed

Source: R/patterns.R
vp_robustness.Rd

Robustness: remove the most required features one at a time and see how much of the skeleton survives. With strategy = "random" the features are removed at random instead, which gives the baseline.

Usage

vp_robustness(model, steps = 5, strategy = c("hubs", "random"), seed = 1)

Arguments

model

A model, from vp_generate() or vp_read(), in its complete or its minimal form.

steps

How many features to remove.

strategy

"hubs" removes the most required features first; "random" removes them at random (the baseline).

seed

The seed of the random numbers, so that the result can be repeated. The random state of the session is left as it was.

Value

A tibble with removed (how many), feature (the one removed at that step), links_left (arrows of the skeleton among the remaining features) and largest_piece (features in the largest connected piece).

See also

Other patterns: vp_baseline(), vp_communities(), vp_compare_groupings(), vp_coreness(), vp_cut_features(), vp_feature_groups(), vp_independent_parts(), vp_odd_ones(), vp_power_law(), vp_similar_features(), vp_triangle_significance(), vp_triangles()

Examples

band <- vp_generate(vp_example("miband3.uvl"), or_graph = TRUE)
vp_robustness(band, steps = 3)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 4
#>   removed feature         links_left largest_piece
#>     <int> <chr>                <dbl>         <dbl>
#> 1       0 NA                       6             7
#> 2       1 Screen                   4             4
#> 3       2 HeartRateSensor          3             3
#> 4       3 BLEv42                   2             2
